theme_measure_sec <- function() {
  ggplot2::theme_bw(base_size = 10, base_family = "sans") +
    ggplot2::theme(
      panel.grid.minor = ggplot2::element_blank(),

## Scope

This vignette demonstrates area-based protein SEC summaries with
`sec_protein`, a synthetic dataset of monoclonal-antibody-like chromatograms.
The embedded component percentages and nominal species sizes describe the
dataset's simulation. They are not experimental measurements or acceptance
criteria.

The dataset does not include protein calibration standards. Its nominal masses
are approximately 600 kDa for HMW aggregates, 300 kDa for dimers, 150 kDa for
monomer, and 50 kDa for fragments. These values are generation assumptions,
not MW estimates recovered from the plotted signal. A polystyrene calibration
curve should not be used to assign protein MW.

## View the synthetic chromatograms

```{r setup}
library(measure)
library(measure.sec)
library(recipes)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(tidyr)
```

```{r protein-data}
data(sec_protein, package = "measure.sec")

chromatograms <- sec_protein |>
  filter(sample_id %in% c("mAb-Reference", "mAb-Stressed-2")) |>
  group_by(sample_id) |>
  mutate(relative_uv = uv_280_signal / max(uv_280_signal, na.rm = TRUE)) |>
  ungroup()

sample_metadata <- sec_protein |>
  distinct(sample_id, description, monomer_pct, dimer_pct, hmw_pct, fragment_pct)

sample_metadata
```

The chart scales each trace to its own maximum to compare peak positions and
shapes. The normalized signal is not an estimate of species percentage.

```{r chromatogram-comparison, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4.5, fig.cap = "Full-range synthetic UV 280 nm traces for the reference and heat-stressed samples, each divided by its own maximum signal. Both show one dominant broad peak near 16 minutes and low signal elsewhere; area-based percentages are calculated separately below.", fig.alt = "Line chart from about 5 to 30 minutes of UV 280 nm signal normalized to each synthetic sample's own maximum. The mAb-Reference and mAb-Stressed-2 traces almost overlap, with one dominant broad peak near 16 minutes and signal near baseline on either side. Each trace is normalized separately, so the y values do not compare sample concentration or area-based component percentages."}
ggplot(
  chromatograms,
  aes(x = elution_time, y = relative_uv, colour = sample_id)
) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.65) +
  scale_colour_manual(
    values = c("mAb-Reference" = "#2E86AB", "mAb-Stressed-2" = "#A23B72")
  ) +
  labs(
    x = "Elution time (min)",
    y = "Relative UV 280 nm signal (maximum = 1)",
    colour = "Synthetic sample"
  ) +
  theme_measure_sec()
```

## Area-based aggregate summary

`step_sec_aggregates()` divides the baseline-corrected signal into HMW,
main-peak, and LMW regions. The boundaries are inferred from the chromatogram
unless explicit limits are supplied. This example reports the step's
calculated area percentages for all five synthetic samples.

```{r aggregates-workflow}
rec_aggregates <- recipe(
  uv_280_signal + elution_time ~ sample_id,
  data = sec_protein
) |>
  update_role(sample_id, new_role = "id") |>
  step_measure_input_long(
    uv_280_signal,
    location = vars(elution_time),
    col_name = "uv"
  ) |>
  step_sec_baseline(measures = "uv") |>
  step_sec_aggregates(
    measures = "uv",
    method = "tallest"
  )

result_aggregates <- prep(rec_aggregates) |>
  bake(new_data = NULL)

result_aggregates |>
  select(sample_id, purity_hmws, purity_monomer, purity_lmws)
```

## Protein summary with `step_sec_protein()`

With `include_oligomer = FALSE`, the step returns three area partitions. The
output is useful for reviewing the main-peak and surrounding signal areas; it
does not produce a calibrated molecular-weight distribution.

```{r protein-workflow}
rec_protein <- recipe(
  uv_280_signal + elution_time ~ sample_id,
  data = sec_protein
) |>
  update_role(sample_id, new_role = "id") |>
  step_measure_input_long(
    uv_280_signal,
    location = vars(elution_time),
    col_name = "uv"
  ) |>
  step_sec_protein(
    measures = "uv",
    type = "native",
    baseline_method = "linear",
    include_oligomer = FALSE
  )

result_protein <- prep(rec_protein) |>
  bake(new_data = NULL)

result_protein |>
  select(sample_id, protein_hmws_pct, protein_monomer_pct, protein_lmws_pct)
```

```{r protein-fractions, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4.5, fig.cap = "HMW, main-peak, and LMW area percentages returned by `step_sec_protein()` for each synthetic sample. Each panel uses its own vertical scale to keep the smaller fractions legible.", fig.alt = "Faceted dot chart of sample ID versus area percentage, with separate panels for HMW, main peak, and LMW signal. Each point is the value returned by `step_sec_protein()` for one of the five synthetic samples. The panels use separate vertical scales; missing values, if present, are left unplotted rather than treated as zero."}
protein_fraction_data <- result_protein |>
  select(sample_id, protein_hmws_pct, protein_monomer_pct, protein_lmws_pct) |>
  pivot_longer(
    cols = starts_with("protein_"),
    names_to = "region",
    values_to = "percent"
  ) |>
  mutate(
    region = recode(
      region,
      protein_hmws_pct = "HMW area",
      protein_monomer_pct = "Main-peak area",
      protein_lmws_pct = "LMW area"
    ),
    sample_id = factor(sample_id, levels = unique(sec_protein$sample_id))
  )

ggplot(protein_fraction_data, aes(x = sample_id, y = percent)) +
  geom_point(
    aes(colour = region),
    size = 2.2,
    na.rm = TRUE
  ) +
  facet_wrap(~region, ncol = 1, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_colour_manual(
    values = c(
      "HMW area" = "#A23B72",
      "Main-peak area" = "#2E86AB",
      "LMW area" = "#3B7A57"
    ),
    guide = "none"
  ) +
  labs(
    x = "Synthetic sample",
    y = "Area percentage (%)"
  ) +
  theme_measure_sec() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 30, hjust = 1))
```

The provided `monomer_pct`, `dimer_pct`, `hmw_pct`, and `fragment_pct` columns
are simulation metadata. They are not outputs from the recipe above. Compare
them only when evaluating the synthetic example; keep the calculated step
results and the dataset's supplied fields distinct.

## Standards and mass assignment

The package's `sec_triple_detect` example includes polystyrene standards, not
protein standards. `step_sec_conventional_cal()` fits a polymer-specific curve;
its output should not be transferred to these protein traces. The
`step_sec_protein()` workflow above reports area regions and does not supply a
protein-standard MW calibration.

For a protein-specific MW estimate, use appropriate protein standards or a
validated method with the calibration information required for that method.
The examples here do not establish suitability or product specifications.
